The variation with temperature of the resistance of a thermistor is shown in Fig. 8.1.

[[fig:f1]]

A student includes the thermistor and an ideal operational amplifier (op-amp) in the circuit of Fig. 8.2.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calculate the potential V⁺ at the non-inverting input of the op-amp.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
At 10 °C, the resistance of the thermistor is 2.5 kΩ.

State and explain whether the light-emitting diode (LED) is emitting light.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain why the student’s circuit will not indicate any change in temperature above 0 °C.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The resistor of resistance 5.0 kΩ is changed to a resistor of resistance R so that the LED switches on or off at a temperature of 20 °C.

Determine R in kΩ.

figures.caption: Fig. 8.1
figures.alt: A graph shows thermistor resistance decreasing with temperature.

figures.caption: Fig. 8.2
figures.alt: A circuit contains a thermistor and resistors connected to an operational amplifier and an LED.
